Tech Scan: Verification

Choose evidence that a change meets its requirements, then give the decision owner its limits.

Draft research reference; published documentation is not a local deployment test. No local pilot or representative-reader study has been completed.

On this page
Separate evidenceBuild a credible checkChoose a candidateDiagnose and hand offSources

Separate evidence

Verification checks an output against specified requirements. Tests exercise expected software behaviour; security scans and adversarial tests seek vulnerabilities; evaluations assess defined agent or AI behaviours across cases. A green result in one category does not replace the others or establish fitness for every use.

For a code change, the engineer records the revision, acceptance criteria, test cases and expected results, CI output, security findings and unresolved failures. For a product containing AI, add evaluation cases for the model, retrieval and tool behaviour where applicable. Workflows & factories covers the authoring and CI handoff; Delivery covers release controls.

Build a credible check

An oracle is the basis used to judge a result: for example, an independently reviewed expected answer, an invariant or a domain expert’s rubric. Independence is a matter of degree, not a second process or a different model name alone.

  • Oracle: have a qualified reviewer derive expected outcomes from requirements and inspect whether the test can catch a wrong result; author-written tests remain useful but are not sufficient alone.
  • Data: reserve held-out cases from the author and tuning loop. Select representative normal, boundary, adverse and no-answer cases from the intended population; protect sensitive data and refresh cases when exposed. A small convenient set does not establish representativeness.
  • Execution: run a separate controlled harness against the exact revision, with pinned configurations and protected results. Separation alone does not make a flawed oracle independent.
  • Decisions: a qualified person who did not author the change reviews failures and evidence; the authorised human retains the release decision. Separate review from action approval.

Model judges can exhibit position, verbosity and self-preference biases. Compare a sample with expert labels, swap ordering for pairwise comparisons and repeat borderline cases; record disagreement. A different model family is not proof of independence, and a judge score alone is not acceptance evidence.[5]

Use formal models for state and concurrency risks

For a race-prone operation, a model checker or proof assistant can help test invariants that example-based tests may miss. Ask an agent to propose a small Lean or TLA+ model, but have the engineer and domain owner first review its states, assumptions and invariants. An internally consistent proof of the wrong specification does not establish correctness of the implementation. A practitioner reported 16 bug-fix pull requests after modeling parts of an agent SDK; this is a case report, not an independent benchmark or evidence that the whole SDK was formally verified. [11]

  1. State the invariant in business terms, for example: two confirmed bookings must never overlap for the same meeting room.
  2. Model only the relevant actions, such as hold, confirm, cancel and concurrent confirm; review whether the model matches the running system.
  3. Investigate any counterexample in the actual service and reproduce it with an executable test before changing production code.
  4. Retain the reviewed specification, counterexample, reproduction and corrected test as evidence; do not substitute the agent's own proof for independent acceptance.

Choose a candidate

AWS-first candidate: trial Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations for agent traces, alongside your own CI tests and security checks. AWS documents on-demand, batch and sampled online evaluation, including built-in and custom evaluators; a model judge evaluates against its criteria, not a proof of patch correctness.[1][2] Amazon Inspector Code Security can scan application code, dependencies and infrastructure as code; findings require triage and do not prove absence of vulnerabilities.[3]

AgentCore Evaluations ships 15 built-in evaluators, alongside managed DeepEval and AutoEval evaluators and custom evaluators you define as a judge or Lambda code.[7] The built-ins cover response quality, task and goal completion, tool use, skills and safety, plus ground-truth trajectory checks — none of them runs your test suite or scores whether a patch is correct.[7]

No managed AWS service evaluates code correctness. Deterministic evidence still comes from your own CI: tests run in GitHub Actions or CodeBuild and are recorded as required status checks in GitHub rulesets — the only mechanism that can block a merge. Add mutation testing as the check on AI-written test suites: a coverage number alone does not show the tests would catch a real fault. Workflows & factories covers the authoring and CI handoff.

Do not build new work on Amazon CodeGuru. CodeGuru Security reached end of support on 20 November 2025; after that date the console, service resources and documentation are no longer accessible. The dedicated end-of-support page has itself been removed, and the notice now survives in the AWS SDK API reference.[8] CodeGuru Reviewer has been in maintenance mode since 7 November 2025 and accepts no new repository associations; existing associations keep working. AWS names Amazon Q Developer for code review and Amazon Inspector for code scanning as the replacements.[9] AWS Security Agent is not named as a CodeGuru successor in either notice, so this page does not present it as one.

Bedrock Guardrails Automated Reasoning checks validate a response against natural-language policies using formal logic — but they operate in detect mode only: they return findings and feedback rather than blocking content.[10] They offer no prompt-injection protection, no off-topic detection and no streaming, and support English (US) only.[10] Treat a VALID result as evidence about the policy you wrote, not as a safety gate.

Conditional alternative: for a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline needing separately controlled evaluation, trial Ragas with approved models and data handling. Compare relevant retrieved material and ranking using context precision and recall, then assess whether answers are faithful to that material. Faithfulness to retrieved text is not truth if the source is stale or wrong; confirm claims against authoritative records.[4][6] Choose the alternative when its metrics and operating model fit better; the team owns its deployment and configuration. Context covers source access and retrieval boundaries.

Hard gates before either pilot: verify required capability, region and availability, approved model and API, data location and retention across traces and judge calls, identity and authorisation, security boundaries, cost and an accountable operator. Stop when a gate is failed or unknown; AWS preference is not an exception. Vendor documentation establishes a capability, not local effectiveness.

Diagnose and hand off

Before running the held-out set, the engineer and domain reviewer agree case selection, expected outcomes, severity and decision thresholds. Record the number passed and total, case mix, model and dataset versions, sampling method, judge disagreement and unresolved failures. A high aggregate cannot override a failed critical requirement; a small sample limits confidence.

Inspect failed traces: was the required source missing, inaccessible or stale; did retrieval rank it poorly; or did generation ignore good evidence? Record the observed failure before proposing a cause. Reproduce, route the issue to its owner and rerun the affected cases and regression set after a fix. Quarantine a flaky check for investigation, but do not silently waive a required gate.

Worked example

Interpret a critical failure

See why an aggregate cannot override a critical failure.

In a fictional pilot, a search assistant passes 18 of 20 held-out cases, but one failure exposes another user’s document. The reviewer records 18/20 and the access failure, blocks the proposed acceptance and sends isolation for investigation; the aggregate does not cancel the critical failure. After repair, rerun isolation and regression cases. An authorised person separately decides whether to release under Path to production.

Public benchmarks can screen options, not establish local acceptance. Results here are not locally validated; inspect service region, data terms, evaluator model, costs and current documentation before adoption.

Do not treat screening as acceptance

Do not let a screening signal, a self-graded check or a detect-only control stand in for acceptance evidence. Use the replacement named in each row.

Evidence that does not establish acceptance
Do not useWhyUse instead
Amazon CodeGuru Security or CodeGuru Reviewer for new workSecurity reached end of support 20 November 2025; Reviewer in maintenance mode since 7 November 2025, with no new repository associations.[8][9]Q Developer for code review; Inspector Code Security for scanning.
A single benchmark number as acceptance evidencePublic benchmarks screen options; they do not establish local acceptance.Your own held-out cases, with the denominator and sampling beside every threshold; see Diagnose and hand off.
A judge from the same model family as the sole acceptance signalPosition, verbosity and self-preference biases.[5]A different model family or a deterministic check alongside; see Build a credible check.
An author agent's own tests or self-review as release evidenceThe author grading itself is not independent validation.A separate harness, held-out cases and a qualified reviewer; see Build a credible check.
A screening eval quoted as a release gateA cheap screen is not a release gate; a gate needs the full held-out set and human review of failures.Full held-out set, deterministic checks and human review; see Diagnose and hand off.
Guardrails Automated Reasoning as a blocking control or prompt-injection protectionDetect mode only; no prompt-injection protection.[10]Content filters and topic policies for blocking; Automated Reasoning findings as feedback.

Gaps and open questions

No managed AWS service evaluates code correctness. Nothing managed runs your test suite, scores patch quality or proves a fix; that is CI plus rulesets plus mutation testing, composed by you.

No managed AWS DAST service exists. Inspector Code Security is static analysis; Security Agent pentesting is per-run and agent-driven. Repeatable dynamic testing of a running app is an open-source scanner you operate.

AgentCore Evaluations general-availability date and region availability are not stated here: the reported 31 March 2026 date comes from secondary sources only.[7]

AWS Security Agent pentesting general availability (reported 31 March 2026, six regions) is not verified against a primary AWS announcement, and the Agent is not named as a CodeGuru successor in the end-of-support notices.[9]

Built-in evaluator count: this page cites the AWS Machine Learning Blog (10 November 2026), which lists 15 built-in evaluators.[7] An older AgentCore README lists 13; re-count with the ListEvaluators API at adoption.

The Automated Reasoning "up to 99%" verification-accuracy figure is a vendor claim whose scope was not verified; it is not quoted on this page.[10]
